wu: Students play 'Routine Race' in pairs. One student mimes a daily routine action (e.g., brushing teeth), the other guesses 'You brush your teeth in the morning'. Swap roles.
wuAlt: Students do a quick 'Find Someone Who' survey with prompts like 'Find someone who wakes up early' and write names.
Teacher shows flashcards of routine actions, students race to shout the time expression (e.g., 'at 7 o'clock' for 'wake up').
pres: Teacher projects a weekly schedule with color-coded weekdays (blue) and weekends (green). Models sentences: 'On weekdays, I wake up at 6 o'clock. At weekends, I wake up at 9 o'clock'. Checks understanding with thumbs up/down for true/false statements.
presAlt: Teacher tells a short story about 'Fatima's Week' using a picture timeline, highlighting weekday/weekend differences.
Students sort picture cards into 'weekday' or 'weekend' piles, then make sentences with 'On weekdays/At weekends I...'.
prac: Students play 'Routine Bingo' in teams. Each team gets a bingo grid with times/actions (e.g., '8:00 - breakfast', 'Saturday - football'). Teacher calls out sentences like 'At weekends, I play football', teams mark the grid.
pracAlt: Students do 'Sentence Scrambles' in pairs, unjumbling present simple sentences with adverbs (e.g., 'I always / eat / breakfast / at 7am').
Teacher models a 'My Day' chant with claps (e.g., 'I wake up! At 7 o'clock!'), students repeat and add their own routines.
ls: Students listen to a recording of two teens talking about their routines. They fill in a table with times/actions for weekdays vs weekends. Teacher plays twice, then checks answers in pairs.
re: After break, students play 'Action Charades'. One student mimes a routine action (e.g., 'go to school'), others shout 'He/She goes to school!'. Fast-paced and physical.
prod: In teams, students conduct a 'Routine Survey'. They interview 3 classmates using prompts like 'What time do you wake up on weekdays?'. They tally results and present findings to the class (e.g., 'Two students wake up at 7 o'clock').
rw: Students read a short text about 'Ahmed's Weekend' and circle all the time expressions. Then, they write 3 sentences about their own weekend using 'at' and 'on' (e.g., 'On Saturday, I go to the market at 10am').
st: Teacher sings a modified 'This is the Way We Brush Our Teeth' song with weekday/weekend verses. Close with: 'Today we compared weekday and weekend routines. Thank you, class!'
g: Students race to write 5 weekday routines on the board in 1 minute.
Students walk around asking 'Find someone who eats lunch at 1pm' and write names.
Teams mark routines called by teacher; first to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Students mime routines; others guess using present simple sentences.
Teams interview classmates; fastest to tally results wins points.
diff: Fast finishers write a paragraph comparing their weekday and weekend routines (40-50 words).
Support learners use a sentence frame: 'On weekdays, I ___ at ___. At weekends, I ___ at ___.'
hw: Interview a family member about their daily routines in English and write 3 sentences.
Draw a picture of your weekday routine and label 5 activities with times.
Write a short paragraph (30 words) about what you do on Saturdays.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references (e.g., 'Friday prayers' for weekend routines) to make the theme relatable. Encourage code-switching to Darija for clarification if needed, but insist on English output.
